semiconductors.summary: The semis cluster is deeply bifurcated — memory names (MU, SNDK, 000660.KS) have been crushed on China competition fears but are now bouncing, while logic/foundry names (NVDA, ASML, TSM) are near support. Cluster stance: earnings validate spend, but prices have run ahead — wait for consolidations.

active_risks.text: Strait of Hormuz disruption — oil elevated at $84.67 as Houthi and US-Iran tensions persist, though a ceasefire framework has been proposed.
US-China AI sanctions and chip war — domestic Chinese DUV scanner in low-volume production, CXMT IPO repriced memory competition, and new forced-labour tariffs escalate trade friction.
China critical materials controls — helium export prohibition in force, rare-earth and Ga/Ge suspensions set to expire in Nov 2026, adding supply-chain uncertainty for semis and power semis.
Fed hawkish hold with three dissents — rate-hike risk persists, keeping borrowing costs elevated for capex-intensive AI names; 10Y at 4.74%.

geopolitical.market_impact: Oil near $85 is feeding inflation fears and keeping the Fed hawkish, which pressures rate-sensitive growth names. The China chip competition repricing has hit memory stocks hardest (MU -15% from highs, SNDK -40% in a month), but hyperscaler capex confirmations are rebuilding the demand case. Semis are oversold, and the VIX at 16 suggests complacency about geopolitical tail risks.

base.description: Hormuz stalemate holds, WTI hovers $80-90. Hyperscaler capex stays elevated through Q3 prints, validating AI demand. Semis consolidate near current levels, with memory and logic names carving a bottom. Fed holds, no hike in September. SPY grinds sideways.

optimistic.description: Ceasefire in the Strait of Hormuz and a US-China trade truce on AI. Oil drops below $75, easing inflation, Fed signals a pause. pessimistic.description: Hormuz escalation resumes, WTI spikes above $100. China retaliates with broader chip sanctions or blocks rare-earth exports. Hyperscaler capex guidance is cut at Q3 prints due to financing stress. Semis sell off further, with memory and neocloud names leading losses.

wildcard.description: A major AI safety incident or regulatory action (e.g., EU bans open-weight models) triggers a broad AI capex repricing. Energy markets spike on a non-Hormuz event (e.g., Saudi supply disruption). Equity indexes drop 10-15% in weeks.
